title: SKY staking rewards are paid from Treasury revenue rather than from new token issuance
content:
A.4.4.1.2.1.1 states that "USDS rewards and SKY rewards for SKY stakers are funded from the Staking Rewards allocation of the Sky Treasury Management Function ... and distributed continuously, pro-rata based on the SKY stake of eligible wallets. Distribution parameters are updated at each Monthly Settlement Cycle."

This is the staking-side consequence of Sky's no-new-emissions rule. Staking yield in most token systems is inflationary — holders are paid in newly minted supply, which is a transfer from non-stakers to stakers dressed up as a return. Here the reward budget is an *allocation of revenue* competing with other uses of the same Treasury Management Function output, including the buybacks that burn SKY.

That makes staking yield structurally honest and structurally constrained: it can only be as large as the protocol's earnings permit, and every unit paid to stakers is a unit not spent burning supply or accumulating reserves. Sky is choosing between two ways of returning value to SKY holders — direct yield to stakers versus scarcity for all holders — rather than manufacturing yield.

The cadence split is the operational detail that makes it work. Accrual is continuous so users are not exposed to snapshot timing, while the *parameters* governing distribution move only at the Monthly Settlement Cycle. Revenue arrives lumpily and must be reconciled periodically; users experience a smooth rate that steps once a month.
description: The Staking Rewards allocation of the Treasury Management Function funds USDS and SKY rewards, distributed continuously pro-rata, with parameters reset each Monthly Settlement Cycle.
